summary: Virtualised scroll view with optional curved layouts, instantiating only what is visible.
overview: Only ever instantiates enough cells to cover the visible viewport plus a small buffer, no matter how large the item count, recycling them as the index range moves. Distinct from the lightweight snap scroll, which does neither virtualisation nor curves.
useCases: A list of thousands of items that must scroll smoothly.
A carousel where cells scale and fade toward the edges.
Any list where instantiating every row would be too slow.

params.tuning: A prefab, not a scene object — it is cloned into the pool.
Extra cells kept beyond the visible count so they are not created mid-scroll. Two or three is usually enough; more just costs memory.
Carousel mode uses the two carousel settings; the others ignore them.

gotchas.title: Cells are recycled, so never store state on them
gotchas.body: The same cell object represents different items as you scroll. All state belongs in your data, applied in the update callback.

gotchas.title: Uniform cell size
gotchas.body: Virtualisation needs to know where each cell is without measuring it. Variable heights are what the masonry layout is for.
